mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% (current value: 1.91%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS <= 2.0% are not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.5% (current value: 1.91%) signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates for equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% are not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0% and GDP (GDPC1) growth is above 1.0% annualized (current UNRATE=3.9%, GDPC1=18507.2), the labor market is tight and economic growth is strong, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in UNRATE<4.0% AND GDPC1>18500 regime are not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 250, current FEDFUNDS=1.91%, CPIAUCSL=251.286), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising interest rates and inflation concerns.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in FEDFUNDS>2.0% AND CPIAUCSL>250 regime are not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4.5% (current value: 3.9%), it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in UNRATE>4.5% periods are not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105 (current value: 107.9989), it signals a weakening economy that reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in INDPRO<105 periods are not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1150 (current value: 1173.0), it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in HOUST<1150 periods are not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a labor market tightening cycle (defined by UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 149000, current UNRATE=3.9%, PAYEMS=149128.0), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 20 trading days due to strong employment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in UNRATE<4.0% AND PAYEMS>149000 regime are not significantly positive (p>0.05).
